_comment: Which Nexus Mods file each release tag publishes to. Read by tools/nexus-target.py,
which the `nexus` job in .github/workflows/release.yml runs.
Both packages live on ONE mod page, crimsondesert/mods/3369, as its own file: the
DesertTooling ASI and the DMM pack, both under Main. So game_scoped_id is the same
for both and file_id is what tells them apart.
desert-tooling's file_id is empty because its file does not exist on the page yet.
It is the merge of the three plugins that used to ship separately (Desert Looter,
Desert Gatherer and Desert Overlay, one .asi each), and the Upload API cannot create
a file - see the last paragraph. Create it by hand on the Files tab, once, then paste
its GroupID here; until then a desert-tooling tag still cuts a GitHub release and the
nexus job simply skips. The three old files stay on the page as archived downloads;
they are not update targets any more and have no entry here.
game_scoped_id  the number in the page URL, e.g. 3369 in
https://www.nexusmods.com/crimsondesert/mods/3369
file_id         the GroupID shown by that file's 'API info' link on the Files tab.
In this API the update group IS the mod file: the persistent file whose
versions form the update chain. It does not change when you upload a new
version, unlike the legacy v1 per-version file number. Or ask the API:
MOD=$(curl -s -H "apikey: $NEXUS_API_KEY" \
https://api.nexusmods.com/v3/games/crimsondesert/mods/3369 | jq -r .data.id)
curl -s -H "apikey: $NEXUS_API_KEY" \
https://api.nexusmods.com/v3/mods/$MOD/files | jq '.data.mod_files[] | {id, name}'
display_name    the file's name on the page. Kept WITHOUT the version, because the
Files tab has its own version column and these names are what the
page's descriptions refer to. {version} is substituted if used.
category        main | optional | miscellaneous, matching where the file sits now.
update_mod_version  whether this file's version becomes the PAGE's version. One page,
two files, so at most one target may set this, or unrelated version
numbers fight over the same field. The DesertTooling ASI is what the
page is about and wins it; the DMM pack is versioned x.y off
dmm_pack.json and would drag the page backwards.
changelog       whether the CHANGELOG entry is appended to the page's changelog. The
page's changelog is keyed by version string and is additive, so both
files can write to it without overwriting each other.
Leave file_id empty for a package that should not go to Nexus. Its tag still cuts a
GitHub release; the nexus job just skips it.
The Upload API adds a new VERSION to a file that already exists. It cannot create a mod
page or the first file on one; those are done by hand on the site, once.
